messages.content: i really liked the film i saw last night, but i do not want to watch it again today.
that can be true. you can enjoy something once and still choose not to do it again right away.
my friend thinks i must not have liked it enough.
you can like a film and still want a different kind of day next. what would you rather do today?
i want to walk outside and think about the story for a while.
then you can keep thinking about the film as part of your day without putting it on the screen again.
give me a shorter answer.
you can think about the film while walking, even if you do not watch it again.
i do not want to explain every detail to my friend. write a short reply.
i enjoyed the film. today i would rather go for a walk, but i would like to talk about the story another time.
can i leave out another time if i am not sure i will want to talk?
yes. do not add another plan just to make the answer sound kind. you could simply say you enjoyed the film and want a walk today.
give me only that message.
i enjoyed the film. today i would rather go for a walk.
is the sun a star?
yes. the sun is a star.
is the moon a star too?
no. the moon is not a star. it is a different kind of object in space.
can i say the moon and sun are both the same because i see them in the sky?
no. being seen in the sky does not make two things the same kind of object.
what about the earth? is that where we live?
yes. the earth is where we live.
write a short example story with a child looking at the sky, but do not make the child walk on the sun.

a child stood by a window and looked at the evening sky. the moon was above the house. she asked her father whether the sun was a star, and he said yes. then she drew the sky in her book before going to bed.
did looking at the moon mean she left the earth?
no. she was by the window in the story. looking at something far away does not mean going there.
just give me the answer about the sun again.
the sun is a star.
i work in an office. the meeting was in the large room, but now it is in the small room by the kitchen. i need to tell another worker without making the message too long.
you could write: the meeting is now in the small room by the kitchen, not the large room.
should i tell them the time changed too?
only if it did. you have told me the room changed, but you have not said anything about a new time.
the time is still the same. add that clearly.
the meeting is now in the small room by the kitchen. the time is the same.
why did you not say it is a different meeting?
because you told me about a change to the room for one meeting. a different room does not by itself mean it is a different meeting.
give me a shorter explanation.
you told me the place changed. you did not tell me there was a new meeting.
now make the message sound like i am talking to another worker by the door.
the meeting is in the small room by the kitchen now. same time as before.
just give me the short message once more.
the meeting is in the small room by the kitchen now. same time as before.
my teacher asked me to write a story about my grandmother. i wrote that she likes tea, has a garden, and reads books. is that a story yet?
those are facts about her, but they do not yet tell what happened. you could choose one visit or one small moment and say what happened in order.
help me with a simple start.
one afternoon, i went to see my grandmother while she was reading by the window.
i remember that she put her book down and asked me to help carry food to the garden.
that gives the next part. you could tell what you carried and what you did outside, rather than only giving a list of things she likes.
i carried bread, and she carried tea. we sat under a tree.
then you have a small story in order: you visited, she asked for help, you carried bread, and you sat outside together.
write the short story from those facts.

one afternoon, i visited my grandmother while she was reading by the window. she put her book down and asked me to help carry food to the garden. i carried bread, and she carried tea. we sat under a tree together.
what new details did you leave out?
i did not add a new reason for the visit or a conversation you had not told me about.
i know one hand and two hands. what is the word for more than one foot?
feet. you can say one foot and two feet.
what is the word for more than one tooth?
teeth. you can say one tooth and two teeth.
can you put feet and hands in one full sentence?
the child put her hands on the table and kept her feet on the floor.
use only our simple words. i want another sentence about a person drawing.
a boy drew two feet and two hands in his picture.
is every word for more than one object made in the same way?
no. foot and feet, tooth and teeth, and hand and hands are different examples of how words can change.
give me just the examples with foot and tooth.
one foot, two feet. one tooth, two teeth.
just give me those two examples again.
one foot, two feet. one tooth, two teeth.
what if i am only asking about grammar, not my real body?
then those examples do not tell me anything about your body. they show how the words are used.
my friends are going to dance, and i would like to join them. i do not know how to do the whole dance yet.
you can want to join and still be learning. could you ask someone to show you a small part first?
give me a plan using one step at a time.
you could ask someone to show you one step at a time and go slowly while you try.
i do not want to say i know the whole dance when i do not.
then be clear about that. you could say: i would like to join, but i need help learning the first part.
what if they are already moving fast?
you can ask whether there is time for a slow try, or watch for a while before you join. you do not have to say you know more than you do.
give me a simple question.
could you show me the first part slowly before we do it together?
write one kind answer a friend could give.
yes. we can try one part at a time, and you can ask me to go slowly.
does that mean i will know everything today?
no. it gives you a way to begin, not a reason to say all the learning will be finished today.
i usually ask for coffee, but today i want tea. the person making breakfast already knows what i usually choose.
you can say the change before the drink is made. for example: could i have tea today instead of coffee, please?
what if they say i thought you liked coffee?
you can say you still like it but want tea today. a choice for one morning does not have to change your general taste.
write that reply.
i still like coffee. i would just like tea this morning, please.
can you tell me tea is always better?
not from this conversation. you asked for help saying your choice, not for a rule that everyone should choose the same drink.
use only our words and keep the answer short.
you can choose tea today without saying it is better for everyone.
now i want to ask for water too. add that to the first question.
could i have tea instead of coffee today, and some water too, please?
what did too add there?
it made the water something you want as well as the tea.
i have an old camera that i do not use every day. my cousin says that must mean i should give it away.
not using something every day does not by itself mean you have no reason to keep it. what do you still use it for, if anything?
i use it on family visits, and it was given to me by my grandmother.
then it has a use and a family meaning for you. you can think about those reasons rather than only how often you pick it up.
pick is in our list, but do you know whether i want to keep it?
you have given reasons you might want to keep it, but you have not said your choice yet.
ask me the question.
do you want to keep the camera?
yes. i want a short answer for my cousin.
i do not use it every day, but i still want it for family visits and because it is from my grandmother.
should i say he is wrong about every object just because this one is different?
no. you can explain your choice about this camera without making a rule for everything he has.
tell a story about a child getting ready before a visit. do not give any time from a clock.

a boy knew his uncle would visit after lunch. in the morning, he chose a book to show him and put it on the table. after breakfast, he drew a picture of the garden. while his mother made lunch, he washed his hands and put the drawing by the book. after eating, he went to the window to wait. when his uncle came, the two things he wanted to show were already ready. he did not need to run around looking for them.
what did he put ready first?
the book he wanted to show his uncle.
what did he do while his mother made lunch?
he washed his hands and put the drawing by the book.
can you tell me which minute he drew the picture?
no. the story only puts it after breakfast. it does not give a clock time.
ask me about the order instead.
did he choose the book before or after drawing the picture?
before. now give me only the two things he wanted to show.
a book and a drawing.
did he need to look for them after his uncle came?
no. they were ready on the table.
my sister says i heard you, but i did not understand. are those different things?
yes. hearing the words and knowing what they mean are different parts of a conversation. she may have heard your voice but still need an explanation.
should i just make my voice have more sound?
not always. if she heard the words clearly, more sound may not fix the meaning. you could ask which part was not clear.
write a question i could ask her.
which part would you like me to explain another way?
she says she does not know what i mean by after the visit.
then explain which visit you mean and when it finishes. knowing the visit makes clear what after the visit is about.
give me a more simple explanation.
tell her which visit you mean. then she can understand what after that visit is about.
if she does understand after that, can i say the first answer was a lie?
no. not understanding at first and understanding after an explanation can both be true.
just give me one sentence about that.
she can hear the words first and understand the meaning later.
in my map story, the library is east of the park. the school is west of the park. which way is the library from the park?
east.
which way is the school from the park?
west.
can you tell me which road to take in my real town from that?
no. you gave a simple map story, but not the road or starting place in your real town.
ask me one question that would help with the real town.
where are you starting from?
i do not want help with the real town now. i just want the story. put the places in order from west to east.
the school, the park, and the library.
tell me whether the school and library are both east of the park.
no. in your story, the school is west of the park and the library is east of it.
what fact did you use for the last answer?
you told me which side of the park each place was on.
make that answer shorter.
you gave the side of the park for each place.
my cousin is coming to stay at our house for a few days. i want to send a welcome message, but i do not want to say we can do anything she wants.
you can sound warm while keeping the plans open. say you are happy she is coming and ask what she would enjoy doing together.
write it simply.
we are happy you are coming. is there something you would like us to do together while you are here?
should i add we will go to any place you want?
only if you mean it and can do that. you have not yet chosen every possible place she might ask to go.
give me a shorter answer.
you can ask what she would enjoy before saying yes to a specific plan.
she says she would like to visit the library and see the garden. both are easy for us.
then you can say those sound like good plans and choose when to go after she gets there.
give me a short reply.
the library and garden sound good. we can choose when to go after you get here.
what did i not say in that reply?
you did not say yes to every possible plan.
in a story, a girl chooses to leave a letter closed. does that tell me the person who wrote the story never reads a letter?
no. what a person does inside a story does not by itself tell us what the person who wrote it does in real life.
say the same idea another way.
a person in a story can leave a letter closed. that does not tell us what the person who made the story does with a real letter.
can i still ask why the girl did not open it?
yes. that is a question about her choice in the story. you would look for the reasons the story gives.
what if no reason is given?
then you can say the story leaves that part open. you can have an idea, but it should not be called a fact the story clearly gives.
give me a short answer.
you can have an idea, but the story has not given a reason as a fact.
write a question that keeps the difference clear.
does the story say why she left the letter closed, or is that my own idea?
there are four people at the table. two want tea, one wants milk, and one wants water. do i need four cups of tea?
no. you need two cups of tea, one cup of milk, and one cup of water, if each person wants one cup.
why did you not give everyone tea just because i said four people?
because the drink choices were different. the number of people does not tell us everyone wants the same drink.
now the person who wanted milk asks for water instead. what should i make?
two cups of tea and two cups of water.
what if one person wants another cup later?
then you can add it when they ask. the first order does not tell us who will want more later.
can i say there are five people because someone asks for another cup?
no. one person can have more than one cup. the number of cups is not always the number of people.
write one short sentence about how many people and cups were in the first order.
there were four people, and each wanted one cup, making four cups.
just give me the drinks after the change.
two cups of tea and two cups of water.
i study a book by reading the whole page again and again. i still do not know which parts i understand.
you could try putting the book down and telling me about one small part in your own words. that can help you see what you remember and what needs another look.
what could i do with one sentence?
read one sentence, put the book down, and say its meaning in your own words.
what if i can write it down but cannot explain it?
then you can write the words without yet understanding the meaning. you can look at a smaller part or ask a question about what is not clear.
give me that answer more simply.
you can know how to write the words without yet understanding the whole meaning. ask about the part that is not clear.
should i change to another book right away?
not just from that one sentence. you could first try a smaller part and see whether a different explanation helps.
write a question for my teacher.
could you explain this part with a simple example?
what goal did i keep the same?
you still want to understand the book. you changed how you work on it.
write about a man who waits for a friend who does not come on time. let him ask what happened before saying the friend does not care.

a man waited by the library for his friend. when the friend did not come at the chosen time, he felt sad and began thinking the visit was not important to her. he took out his phone and asked whether she was still coming. she answered that her first message had said the park, not the library. they looked at the messages and found that they had been waiting in different places. he told her where he was, and they chose one place to meet. they both wanted the visit, but they had not understood the same plan.
give me only the part about what he learned after asking.
he had felt sad, but then learned they were waiting in different places. the visit was still important to both of them.
say the answer in another simple way.
they both wanted the visit, but they had not understood the same meeting place.
was asking a question useful?
yes. it gave them information they did not have while waiting.
what did they need to choose together?
one meeting place.
give the answer as a full sentence.
they needed to choose the same place to meet.
i want to tell my brother i may visit tomorrow, but i do not know yet. can you write it without making it sound sure?
i may visit tomorrow, but i have not chosen yet. i will let you know when i do.
what if i only write i will visit tomorrow?
that would sound like a plan you have chosen, not a choice you still have to make.
give a short explanation.
you have not chosen yet, so it is better to keep may in the message.
can the message still be kind if it does not say yes?
yes. being clear about what you do not know can still be kind. you can say you would like to see him without saying the visit will happen for sure.
write that with like in it.
i would like to see you tomorrow, but i do not know yet whether i can come. i will let you know.
should i say i cannot come if i only do not know?
no. not knowing yet is different from knowing the answer is no.
just give me one sentence that keeps the choice open.
i may visit tomorrow, but i have not chosen yet.
here is the end of my story: the boy left the book on the table and went home. change it so he takes the book home, but keep the rest simple.
the boy took the book and went home.
should you add that he was taking it without being asked?
not unless that is part of your story. taking a book does not by itself tell us whether it is his or whether someone let him use it.
just ask what you need to know before saying he did something wrong.
was the book his to take, or had someone said he could use it?
i want no new facts about that. keep the end simple.
the boy took the book and went home.
what changed from the first end of the story?
the book went home with the boy instead of being left on the table.
give the answer another way.
before, he left the book on the table. now, he took it home.
write one question a person reading the story might still have.
was the book his to take home?
i like playing a small game with my cousin, but i do not care which of us gets the most pieces.
you can enjoy the time together without making who gets the most pieces the important part. what do you like about the game?
i like making choices and seeing what happens next.
then those can be the good parts for you. you do not need to turn every game into a test of who is best.
my cousin likes trying to get more than me. can we still enjoy it together?
you could, if both of you can keep the different reasons in mind. you can tell your cousin that you like the game but do not want it to become a question of who is better as a person.
ask me a simple question instead.
what would make the game feel good for both of you?
i want us to talk and not feel sad if something goes wrong.
you could say: i like playing with you. can we keep it calm and enjoy the game even when one of us does not do well?
just give me that message.
i like playing with you. can we keep it calm and enjoy the game even when one of us does not do well?
i had an idea for a story while walking. now i feel as if i must write the whole thing today or lose it.
you could write a small note about the idea first. keeping the start does not mean you have to finish the whole story today.
what could the note have in it?
you could write who is in the story, where it starts, and one thing that happens. that may be enough to help you return to it later.
i only know there is a child with an old book in a garden.
then that is a useful first note. you do not have to make up the whole end just to keep that picture in your mind.
write my note with no new facts.
a child has an old book in a garden.
is that too little to count as an idea?
no. it is a small idea, and it can stay small until you want to work on it more.
what if tomorrow i want to change the book to a letter?
you can change a story idea. the note helps you remember your first thought without making it a rule you can never change.
write one kind sentence about leaving it for another day.
you can keep the small idea now and return to it when you are ready.
